blocks.text: In 1958 the American biologists Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl tested the three models and showed that DNA replication is semi-conservative.

items: Bacteria were grown on a medium containing the heavy isotope of nitrogen, 15N, which entered the nitrogen bases of their DNA in place of normal 14N; after many generations their DNA was denser than normal.
The bacteria were then moved to a medium containing 14N, so new DNA would be made with 14N, and DNA was collected at intervals as the bacteria divided.

The DNA was dissolved in caesium chloride solution and ultracentrifuged; this forms a density gradient, densest at the bottom, and each kind of DNA settles where its density matches the solution. Denser 15N DNA settles lower than lighter 14N DNA.

blocks.alt: Three centrifuge tubes of caesium chloride. At 0 minutes, one band at the heavy (15N) level. At 20 minutes, after one round of replication in 14N, one band at the hybrid level. At 40 minutes, after two rounds, one hybrid band and one light (14N) band. Under each tube are the DNA molecules that explain it.
blocks.caption: Bands in the caesium chloride tubes and the DNA that explains them (original diagram after Figure 19.9).
blocks.long_description: Meselson and Stahl grew bacteria for many generations in 15N, so their DNA became dense, then moved them to 14N and sampled the DNA as they divided. The DNA was spun in caesium chloride, which forms a density gradient in which each kind of DNA settles where its density matches. Before replication there was one heavy band; after one replication one band of intermediate density, because every molecule was a hybrid of one 15N and one 14N strand; after two replications one hybrid and one light band. This is what the semi-conservative model predicts, and it rules out the conservative model (which would give heavy and light bands after one round) and the dispersive model (which would never give a light band).

blocks.caption: Observations and explanation
rows: each molecule is a hybrid: one 15N strand and one 14N strand
one intermediate and one light band
each hybrid gives one heavy strand to a new hybrid and one light strand to an all-14N molecule

blocks.title: Tracing radio-isotope labelled DNA in the progeny
blocks.text: An experiment in which radio-isotope labelled DNA is traced in an organism's progeny is a pulse-chase experiment. In the pulse stage the organism is exposed to the radio-isotope briefly and builds it into its DNA; in the chase stage the labelled DNA is followed over time by measuring its radioactivity.
